Solution 3 has the correct final answer, $c=3$.

The problem says the new bound refines $n \le 2m-3$, so it must be at least as strong for every $k \ge 3$. That requires $\lfloor (k+c)/2 \rfloor \ge 3$ for all $k \ge 3$, which forces $c \ge 3$ (at $k=3$). With $c=2$, the $k=3$ bound would be $2m-2$, which is weaker than $2m-3$, so it cannot be a refinement. Solution 2 reaches this same constraint but then abandons it for 2.

Solution 3's derivation also gives $j \ge \lceil k/2 \rceil + 1 = \lfloor (k+3)/2 \rfloor$, which matches $2m-3$ at $k=3,4$ and improves it for larger $k$. I checked the consistency of this form with the refinement requirement, not the full geometric argument, so my confidence is somewhat below the maximum.

CHOICE: 3
CONFIDENCE: 4
